# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-07

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
A stranger would close the tab halfway down the page. While the hero section is clean and clear, the page quickly devolves into an overwhelming wall of internal status reports, unanchored acronyms, and literal leaked local filesystem paths that destroy its credibility as a polished product.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Leaked local filesystem paths in production copy (Live benchmark card and CSS font imports).
2. Deep internal jargon used without context (FoVer, CCTU, PREM, TTC).
3. The "Evidence" section is an unfiltered dump of 12 highly specific result cards that overwhelm the reader.

## DETAILED FINDINGS
### Bloat
- Results Grid — 12 cards — Cap at 4-6 of the most impactful, universally understandable metrics.
- Blog/Writing section — 7 cards — Cap at 3 most recent or relevant posts.
- "Recent progress" card under Stats — 61 words — Reads like a blog post or commit message; cap at 30 words or remove entirely.

### Internal jargon
- "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" bento card — `TTC`, `PREM` — These acronyms are undefined in context and read like proprietary lab terminology.
- "Results" section (Live benchmark card) — `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` — Hyper-specific model identifier that looks like an internal naming convention rather than a standard model tag.
- "Stats / Recent Progress" section — `FoVer`, `5-seed dual-condition` — A stranger has no idea what dataset "FoVer" is or what conditions are being tested.
- "Capabilities" section (Typed constraints) — `CCTU constrained tool-use micro-benchmark` — Niche benchmark jargon used without explanation.

### Per-milestone narrative
- "Recent progress" card — "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit; see Why We Report Two AUROCs Now." — This is an internal team status update, not value-proposition copy.

### Inconsistencies
- 0.9131 Verifier AUROC vs 0.8947 vs 0.9857 — The headline stat highlights 0.9131, but the "Recent progress" paragraph immediately introduces two other completely different AUROC numbers for the same feature. A stranger will distrust the metrics when they contradict themselves in the same section.

### Missing essentials
- Direct reproduction links: You claim every number is backed by an artifact, but provide no clickable links from the perfect-looking results cards to those artifacts, asking the user to just take your word for it.

### Fabrication signals
- Live benchmark Result Card — `HumanEval pass @.tmp-pytest/pytest-of-ianblenke/pytest-3/popen-gw0/test_req_verify_2932_run_uses_0/citation_hallucination_field_verifier_2932_raw/spilled-energy-2602-18671:real.txt 0% → 36%` — A literal local test path leaked into the public claim.
- Adversarial audit Result Card — "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100% catch rate on exactly 60 attacks looks artificially perfect.
- Math extraction Result Card — "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — A perfect 1.0 True Positive rate is a massive red flag for overfitting or a broken evaluation pipeline.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero section clearly and concisely explains the core value proposition ("Catch the reasoning errors your LLM states") before descending into jargon.
- The "Quick Start" code tabs are excellent, showing the exact 3-line API in both Python and Rust to prove it's real and usable.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. Immediately remove the leaked local paths (`@.tmp-pytest/...`) from the HTML text in the Live benchmark card and the CSS font-family imports.
2. Delete the "Recent progress" card entirely; move the AUROC methodology clarifications to the Technical Report.
3. Prune the Results grid from 12 cards down to the 4 most impressive, widely understood benchmarks (e.g., HumanEval code repair, general reasoning lift).
4. Remove the "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" bento card, or rewrite it in plain English without the acronyms.
5. Soften perfect 1.0/100% claims (e.g., 60/60 attacks) by explicitly stating the constrained environment, or link the card directly to the open source reproduction artifact.
